title: S007 — Long-horizon semantic state scaling experiment
description: Empirically measure how the corrected P-007 semantic-state architecture behaves under extreme long-horizon counterfactual workloads. Specifically: does the canonical semantic representation remain computationally and memory-efficient as intervention history and world branching grow? P-007 is frozen and must not be modified; all experiment code is isolated.
constraints: Do not modify P-005, S006, frozen P-007, canonical acceptance fixtures, frozen canon hashes, or production semantics.
Record the exact P-007 ancestor commit (443d3d9).
All experiment-specific changes remain isolated to the experiment branch.
Every experiment reproducible from (seed, canon, configuration, software commit).
Do not optimise prematurely; measure first.
The experiment succeeds even if Somnium scales badly, provided the limit is identified and explained.
experiments: B — branching: controlled branch factors and depths; trajectories vs unique states.
C — convergence/collision: different histories reaching equivalent effective worlds.
D — WorldDiff cost: equal / small-delta / large-delta pairwise comparisons.
E — parallel scaling: 1..16 workers, throughput/speedup/efficiency, determinism preserved.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline recorded: test count, pass count, frozen canon hashes, commit, runtime.

Wall-clock, throughput, per-phase timings (canonicalization/representation/hashing/diff/branch-gen), peak RSS, representation size, diff size, branches, unique states, convergent states, genealogy depth, divergence distribution measured where applicable.
Determinism verified: equivalent runs produce identical semantic results and hashes.
Report produced with sections 1-12 (environment, baseline, linear, branching, convergence, WorldDiff, parallel, bottleneck, complexity, resource envelope, findings, recommendation).
Frozen P-007 untouched; src/ has zero diff vs 443d3d9.
result_summary: Canonical semantic representation is BOUNDED (~50KB verrin / ~39KB ordos) and flat from H=1000 to H=100000: stateHash and worldDiff are history-independent. Single-derive is O(H); the chain walk is O(H^2). Parallel scaling peaks at 1.10x on 4 cores and degrades beyond. The only architectural bottleneck is non-incremental derivation.
